chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said:

Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Arafah, recognizing his rights, Allāh will register for him the reward of one thousand Hajj and one thousand ‘Umrah and one thousand battles with a messenger Prophet. And whoever visits on the first day of Rajab, Allāh will forgive him completely.

key_terms.رَجَبٍ: Rajab (the seventh month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically for ziyarah/pilgrimage to a shrine)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for visiting the grave of Imam Husain on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, the Day of ‘Arafah is uniquely significant as the day Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) was martyred, making this ziyārah a commemoration of his ultimate sacrifice and intercession. The multiplication of rewards—thousand-fold for Hajj, Umrah, and Ghazw—underscores the concept of *thawāb al-‘amal* (reward of action) where visiting the Imam is equated to serving the Prophet directly. Furthermore, the first of Rajab is recognized as the day of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s birth, linking the beginning of the month with the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt and the promise of divine forgiveness.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said:

Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Allāh will register the reward of one thousand Hajj and one thousand ‘Umrah and the reward of fighting one thousand times with one of Allāh’s messengers for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the Day of ‘Arafah while knowing his rights. And surely Allāh forgives those who go to his Ziyārah on the first day of Rajab.
